bib.title: Artificial Hippocampus Networks for Efficient Long-Context Modeling

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: all 22 pages (82,247 chars) read, including appendices A-H. References skimmed. No embedded instructions found.

SOURCE: "Artificial Hippocampus Networks for Efficient Long-Context Modeling". Yunhao Fang*, Weihao Yu*(corresponding), Shu Zhong, Qinghao Ye, Xuehan Xiong, Lai Wei, all ByteDance Seed. (*equal contribution; Xiong's work was done while at ByteDance Seed.) arXiv 2510.07318v2, cs.CL, 17 Dec 2025. Preprint; no venue printed. Code: github.com/ByteDance-Seed/AHN.

MAIN CLAIM: Keep a large sliding-window KV cache (32k) as lossless short-term memory. A small learned RNN-like module (the AHN) folds each KV pair that leaves the window into a fixed-size recurrent state. This cuts FLOPs and cache at 128k context while matching or beating full attention on average scores. Below 32k the AHN never activates, so the model is identical to the base model.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
1. LV-Eval 128k, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, AHN-GDN vs full attention: average 4.41 -> 5.88, with 0.4% extra parameters, 40.5% fewer FLOPs, 74.0% less memory cache. Table 2 (Qwen2.5-3B) lists model FLOP ratio 59.4% and cache ratio 26.0% for the AHN rows. Setup: 11 LV-Eval datasets at 128k, 32,768 lossless tokens (128 sinks + 32,640 window). The paper gives no sample counts, seeds or confidence intervals, so differences are small single-run scores.
2. Same table, 7B and 14B (LV-Eval avg): 7B full attention 3.62, sinks+SWA 5.34, AHN-GDN 6.54, AHN-DN 6.83. 14B full attention 4.99, sinks+SWA 5.69, AHN-GDN 6.51. Cache ratio is about 26% for all. AHN beats the equal-memory sliding-window baseline and Compressive Transformer max/avg-pooling baselines throughout. The gain over SWA is about 1 point on LV-Eval for 7B and under 1 point for 14B. InfiniteBench 7B avg: full attention 13.50, SWA 13.16, AHN-GDN 16.93.
3. Exact recall, where full attention wins (Appendix B, Table 5): RULER-128k NIAH, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AHN-GDN vs sinks+SWA vs full attention. single_1: 26.80 / 26.80 / 98.60. single_2: 25.20 / 25.40 / 97.20. single_3: 28.20 / 28.00 / 98.40. multikey_1: 27.40 / 27.80 / 89.20. multiquery: 23.35 / 24.00 / 85.45. AHN is no better than plain SWA on these tasks. Also, LV-Eval factrecall_en on 14B: full 4.31, AHN-GDN 0.15.
4. Training cost: only the AHN parameters (about 0.4%) are trained, base model frozen, by self-distillation (KL to the full-attention teacher). Data is ChatQA2, 1B tokens, 740 steps at batch 128, about 10 hours on 32 A100s for 7B. Ablation (Table 4, Qwen2.5-7B, LongBench avg of 6 tasks): KL with random window 40.59, CE loss 39.59, KL with fixed 1024 window 38.53.

QUOTES
- "AHN-GDN performs on par with sliding window attention but markedly worse than full attention on exact-recall tasks." (p.19, Appendix B)
- "their fixed-size compressed memory inevitably entails some information loss and may impair performance on tasks that require exact recall" (p.10, Conclusion)

LIMITS
- Exact recall is not solved: out-of-window needles are effectively lost on RULER (see number 3). The compressed state adds nothing there.
- Tested only on Qwen2.5-Instruct 3B/7B/14B, and mostly 128k contexts. LongBench was run with an 8k window.
- "Surpassing full attention" is partly because full attention degrades at 128k on these benchmarks. The authors attribute large-window drops to attention dilution, which is a hypothesis. LV-Eval scores are very low in absolute terms (about 4-7).
- This changes the model: it needs trained AHN weights and a custom architecture. It is not a prompt-level or API technique, so it cannot be applied to a hosted closed model.
- Short-context performance is identical to the base model by construction, not measured.
- The gradient-visualisation claim that AHN keeps numbers and symbols (Fig. 5) is one example of 811 tokens.
- Not shown: agent or multi-turn settings, memory across sessions, or comparison against retrieval (RAG).

BUILDS ON
- Multi-Store Memory Model (Atkinson & Shiffrin, 1968).
- Mamba2 (Dao & Gu, 2024), DeltaNet (Schlag et al. 2021; Yang et al. 2024), GatedDeltaNet (Yang et al. 2025).
- Compressive Transformer (Rae et al., 2020) and Transformer-XL (Dai et al. 2019).
- Attention sinks, StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., 2023).
- Attention-RNN hybrids: Infini-attention, LoLCATs, HQLT, MiL. These use small windows (64 to 2048).
- Self-distillation. Benchmarks: LV-Eval, InfiniteBench, LongBench, RULER.
(Years from my knowledge of those works; the extraction prints citations only as numbers, so years are not verified against the text.)

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 2(a), p.4. A window-of-3 diagram showing tokens leaving the window, being folded into the compressed memory and then discarded. It explains the mechanism faster than prose. Alternative: Figure 1(a)/(b), p.1, for the efficiency summary. Fig. 3(a,b), p.5, shows linear FLOPs and constant cache against sequence length.

PROBLEMS: the Table 2 and 6 extraction has run-together numbers (bold and column spacing), so some cells are ambiguous. I used values that parse cleanly. The Table 6 14B loogle_CR row for full attention reads "0.3.64", which is garbled and unused. Extracted text is at /tmp/ahn.txt.
